lesson_title: Lift the Cage, Take the Questions
hook_text: Three board members, a stopwatch, and your cardboard headgear about to lift 300 grams in front of them. Here is how to win a tender.
clip_script: The board is the client, and it hunts for risk. It has a rubric; read it first and spend your seven minutes where the marks are. Walk your six documents: the brief with a fact from your investigation, the working drawing and why this tower, the gear sheet and systems diagram with real numbers in and out, then two minutes of demonstration. Tested on this very table beforehand, checklist ticked, fresh batteries. Say the numbers as it happens: 300 grams, one metre, 15 seconds. Brake at mid-shaft: holding. Sway with a kilogram on top: 6 millimetres. Swing it: no topple. If it fails live, say so and quote the table. Then the method in a sentence and the budget with its total, biggest lines, contingency and sources. Questions: evidence, source and date, never a guess. The flashiest model rarely wins. The one with every document behind it does.
visual_style: Boardroom table on a whiteboard with three figures; a seven-block timeline sized by minutes; the model lifts a cage with a stopwatch overlay and a sway ruler; a budget summary with circled sources; a scorecard fills.
pacing: The board, the six documents, the demo, questions, the decision.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and tape a demonstration checklist to your model's base.
